messages:
incident-bot: PAGER: Elevated error rate and latency observed in eu-west-1 for Hosted API + Dedicated pools. 502/504 spikes and token failures reported. Alert group: infra-auth. Auto-runbooks attached: https://go/reports/3832109876 :rotating_light:

mara (oncall): seeing it in the dashboard. Hosted API 5xx jump ~ 12% -> 22% over last 3m, p95 latency from 180ms -> 900ms. Dedicated pools in eu-west-1 also show request timeouts.

jonathan: confirmed. Tracing shows `auth-token` calls to external token service (AuthX) returning 429/502. Downstream services fail during token exchange. Example trace: `/auth/token -> 502`.

mara (oncall): okay, quick triage: are we hitting an AWS control-plane thing or is this third-party (AuthX) rate-limiting?

jonathan: looks like AuthX (third-party) — many of our token refresh endpoints are failing. curl against their endpoint returns `HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests` and occasional `502`.

sumi: paging AWS status too but initial confirm is external token provider. Posting logs snippet:
```
[2026-03-15T10:32:04Z] token_fetch user=svc-redwood err=HTTP 429 body="rate limit exceeded"
[2026-03-15T10:32:07Z] token_fetch user=svc-redwood err=HTTP 502 backend_error=upstream
```

mara (oncall): impact estimate? Which customers / regions affected?

taylor: impact matrix: customers with pinned Dedicated pools in eu-west-1 and Hosted API customers routed to eu-west-1. Estimated affected requests: ~5-8% of overall traffic but 18-25% for eu-west-1 region. Some mobile customers reporting timeouts. Logging shows spike in customer-facing 504s.

jonathan: replication note — our token cache TTL is short (30s default) for security. Large burst of token refresh requests amplifies calls to AuthX. We should: 1) increase TTL temporarily 2) enable local token fallback cache 3) route new requests to eu-west-2 where possible.

mara (oncall): agree. Immediate mitigations:
- bump token cache TTL to 5m for affected services
- enable local fallback (serve cached token if provider 5xx/429)
- change routing policy for non-PINNED Hosted API customers to prefer eu-west-2
- open ticket with AuthX + contact AWS if we see control-plane issues

jonathan: applying config change to token service now. command:
```bash
rbctl config set service.token_cache.ttl 300 --env prod --region eu-west-1 --reason "AuthX rate limit mitigation"
```

incident-bot: Action logged: config change requested by jonathan. Runbook step 2: Notify customer success for high-visibility customers.

taylor: pinging CS now for top 10 customers in eu-west-1. will post status page note draft.

sumi: rolling TTL change via canary to 2 of 6 nodes in eu-west-1. Monitoring auth failures and 5xx%.

mara (oncall): good. Also prepare routing change for non-pinned traffic. jonathan can you push the region preference rule?

jonathan: pushing routing override:
```bash
rbctl route set-priority --from eu-west-1 --to eu-west-2 --scope hosts=non-pinned --weight=0.7
```
applied to traffic controller. logs show 68% of new connections now preferring eu-west-2.

ops-bot: aws-support-ticket opened: #AWS-89234 (monitoring). AuthX support request created: AUTHX-4578. Contact channel: #authx-status (cc @AuthX_SRE).

mara (oncall): small side-effect: increased latency for some long-haul customers while connections warm in eu-west-2. Keep an eye on p99. If risk to SLAs increases, we'll fallback to cached-only mode.

taylor: statuspage draft ready: "We are investigating elevated errors affecting eu-west-1 due to a third-party token service. Mitigations in progress. Some requests may be delayed or return errors." Will publish after mara approves. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

sumi: auth failures dropping from 22% -> 6% on canary nodes after TTL bump. Good sign. Monitoring full roll-out.

jonathan: note on Dedicated pools: some customers pinned to hardware in eu-west-1 will keep seeing errors until we can failover their pools (requires customer opt-in). For those customers we can enable local token cache fallback and increase retry window to reduce visible 5xx.

mara (oncall): declare incident Sev2 (not a full regional outage, but customer-impacting for a subset). Oncall handoff plan: I'll stay on until 11:15Z, then hand off to sumi (next oncall).

taylor: CS updated top customers, sent targeted messages to two enterprise accounts. Support queue triaged — we flagged high-priority tickets.

jonathan: rolling config to remaining nodes now. Also added exponential backoff to token fetches to reduce thundering herd:
```diff
- retries: 3
+ retries: 6
+ backoff: exponential (base 200ms)
```

sumi: AuthX replied in their channel: "We are experiencing elevated token-service errors in eu-west-1 due to internal throttling. Investigating. ETA unknown." They asked for request traces and sample tx IDs (sent).

mara (oncall): good. continue rollout. prepare for two things in parallel: (A) full roll-out of TTL/backoff + routing pref (B) customer-level mitigations for pinned Dedicated pools (CS + SEs to coordinate).

ops-bot: audit log entry: change by jonathan at 2026-03-15T10:39:12Z - token_cache.ttl=300.

taylor: publishing status page now. message sent.

mara (oncall): summary for handoff to sumi:
- root cause: third-party token provider (AuthX) rate-limiting/throttling in eu-west-1 causing token exchange 429/502s
- current impact: Hosted API non-pinned traffic mitigated by routing to eu-west-2; Dedicated pinned pools still affected unless customers opt-in to failover.
- actions taken: increased token cache TTL to 5m, enabled local fallback serve-on-5xx, rolling backoff/retry config, routing preference to eu-west-2 for non-pinned traffic, CS notified top customers, AuthX ticket opened (AUTHX-4578)
- next steps: finish rollout, monitor p95/p99, coordinate with CS for customer failovers, escalate to AuthX if no improvement in 30m, open AWS ticket if evidence of regional control-plane involvement

sumi: acknowledged. I'll take over at 11:15Z and own until resolved or until further escalation. Please add any additional notes here.

mara (oncall): handing off now. attaching timeline and runbook snippet for next oncall. :white_check_mark:

jonathan: one more: if AuthX doesn't recover, we have an emergency plan to switch to our secondary token provider (requires co-ord, may break some mTLS flows). Prep doc: https://go/runbooks/token-failover.

taylor: continuing CS comms, monitoring inbound.

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: Mitigations applied; auth errors decreased to 5-8% regionally. Incident Sev2. Next update scheduled in 15m.
